what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/book-time: the times a person can be booked (their weekly windows minus what is already booked and what their calendar shows busy), booking one of those times as a record in their own records with a lifecycle, and putting, moving and cancelling the event on the person's own Google calendar with their own account, or making the invitation file for any mail client.

payload.label: Find open times
payload.job: Find the times someone can book with me, from my weekly hours, minus what is already booked and what my calendar shows busy
payload.description: Gives the open start times over one or more days, in the person's time zone. A time is open when it fits wholly inside a weekly window on that weekday, is not a start in the taken list, does not overlap a busy interval (widened by the buffers before and after), and starts after the minimum notice. Bookings given in `bookings` count too (booking records as tool:request-a-booking answered them): a booking fills a seat of the time it starts at and blocks every other time it overlaps (a cancelled booking frees its time); a day closes once per_day_max bookings start on it, and nothing past horizon_days is offered. Windows, lengths, buffers, seats and limits are the person's own: nothing is assumed.

timezone.description: The IANA zone the windows are written in, like "America/Chicago"

end.description: HH:MM in the zone, up to 24:00

from_date.description: The first day, YYYY-MM-DD in the zone

days.description: How many days from from_date (1 when left out)

step_minutes.description: Spacing between offered starts (the duration when left out)

min_notice_minutes.description: A time must start this long after now

busy.description: Busy intervals (instants), like those tool:check-when-i-am-busy gives

host_ref.description: With bookings: only this host's bookings

free_statuses.description: Booking statuses that free their time ("cancelled" when left out)

seats_per_slot.description: How many people may book the same time (1 when left out); each time shows the seats left

per_day_max.description: Once this many bookings start on a day, the rest of that day is not offered

horizon_days.description: Nothing is offered more than this many days from now

pending_blocks_slot.description: Whether a booking waiting for the host to confirm holds its time (true when left out)

bookings.description: The person's existing booking records, read by the AI from wherever the person keeps them; they count as taken

payload.label: Request a booking
payload.job: Check a requested time is open and make the booking record for it
payload.description: Checks that the start asked for is an open time (same rules as tool:find-open-times, with the existing bookings given in `bookings` counted), then answers one booking record; it keeps nothing, so the AI keeps the record where the person keeps bookings. It starts waiting for payment, waiting for the host to confirm, or booked, as the request says. When `bookings` already holds a booking with this idempotency_key, that booking is answered and no new one is made. A time that is not open is refused with the open times that day; a person who already holds a seat at that time is refused a second one.

windows.description: The weekly windows, as in tool:find-open-times

attendees.description: Who is booked, like { name, email }

needs_confirmation.description: Start as waiting for the host to confirm

seats_per_slot.description: How many people may book the same time (1 when left out); one person holds one seat of a time

per_day_max.description: At most this many bookings start on one day

horizon_days.description: A time more than this many days from now is not open

pending_blocks_slot.description: Whether a booking waiting for the host to confirm holds its time (true when left out); when false the time is checked again when the host confirms

bookings.description: The person's existing booking records, read by the AI from wherever the person keeps them; they count as taken

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/calendar-booker (request-booking action and booking-status contract), ported to the records door

payload.label: Change a booking's status
payload.job: Work out a booking's new record for confirming, cancelling, completing or marking a no-show, only in the ways a booking may move
payload.description: Answers the booking record moved to a new status: waiting bookings can be confirmed or cancelled, a confirmed one can be completed, marked no-show or cancelled, and a finished one never moves. A cancel carries its time and reason. Asking for the status it already has changes nothing. A move that is not allowed is refused with the moves that are. It keeps nothing: the AI keeps the answered record. A waiting booking whose time has passed can be cancelled but not confirmed, and one that did not hold its time is confirmed only if the time is still open among the other `bookings` given.

to.description: The new status, like confirmed or cancelled

booking.description: The booking record to move, as the AI read it

bookings.description: The person's other booking records, needed only to confirm a waiting booking that did not hold its time

payload.label: Check when I am busy
payload.job: Read when my own calendar shows me busy between two times
payload.description: Asks the person's own Google calendar when it is busy between two instants, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account). Answers the busy intervals, or unknown with the reason when the calendar cannot be read: unknown is never an empty free answer, so offer no times it guessed. Changes nothing.

payload.label: Put a booking on my calendar
payload.job: Make the event for a booking on my own calendar and invite the people booked
payload.description: Makes one event on the person's own Google calendar, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account), and has Google invite the attendees. A video call is made only when video_call_request_id is given, and is an error when Google made none. It keeps nothing: the AI notes the event's id and call link on the booking where the person keeps it. Answers created and the event's id and link, or error and why.

start_local.description: Wall-clock start in the zone, like 2026-08-12T09:00

video_call_request_id.description: Ask for a video call; the same id asks for the same call

payload.label: Move a booking on my calendar
payload.job: Move a booking's event on my own calendar to a new time
payload.description: Moves one event on the person's own Google calendar to a new start and end, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account); Google tells the attendees. Answers changed, or error and why.

event_id.description: The event's id, as tool:put-a-booking-on-my-calendar gave it

payload.label: Cancel a booking on my calendar
payload.job: Remove a booking's event from my own calendar
payload.description: Deletes one event from the person's own Google calendar, with the person's own calendar account (the held value calendar-account); Google tells the attendees. An event already gone counts as cancelled. Answers changed, or error and why.

payload.label: Make a calendar invite
payload.job: Make an invitation file that any mail client turns into a calendar event, or into a cancellation
payload.description: Writes a standard calendar file (.ics): a request that creates or updates an event, or a cancel that removes it. The host is the organizer, so the host's own calendar shows it, and everyone else is an attendee. The same uid with a higher sequence updates the event. Times are instants, written in UTC. It sends nothing: attach the text to a message.

uid.description: The event's own id; keep it for updates and the cancel

sequence.description: Raise it for every change to the same uid
